title: fix(ui): danger colours render red in both themes; light danger text clears 4.5:1
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-sales"} -->
_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4UuDYM244ZZo7uXksNPNmuEyz)_

Fixes #35911
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 列表和表格导出失败的提示、Markdown 里的「注意」提示框、流程预览里出错的连线，深浅两种主题下都显示为清楚的红色；浅色主题下「删除」等红色文字从亮红调深为深红（对比度 3.76:1 → 6.47:1），红色按钮和徽标的底色不变。
- 这是按你对浅色危险红的裁决（只调深文字到深红）完成整张卡，来自「列表页重做」专题里深色删除按钮那次修复时发现的问题。
- 出错最坏是某处红字的深浅和以前不同；只改颜色，不动数据和流程，可以直接撤回。
- 无

## What changes

**Items 1 and 2 (invalid and non-dark-aware danger colours).**

- `--destructive` holds an HSL triplet (`0 84.2% 60.2%`), so a bare `var(--destructive)` is not a colour and the browser drops the declaration (the `var()` fallback never applies because the variable is defined). The grid's and list's export-error line now drop the inline `style` and use the `text-destructive` utility (which also satisfies the `ui/` no-inline-colour rule). The Markdown caution alert's border and title now read `hsl(var(--destructive-text, var(--destructive)))`, the spelling the Gantt resource view already uses.
- The flow preview's invalid edge (`stroke-destructive`) and its arrowhead marker (`fill-destructive`) read `--color-destructive`, the deep dark-theme button fill. They now paint with `currentColor` under `text-destructive` (`stroke-current text-destructive`, `fill-current text-destructive`), so they follow the dark-aware danger text token from the dark-theme Delete fix. No new theme token: Tailwind 4 resolves `fill-*`/`stroke-*` from `--fill-*`/`--stroke-*` then `--color-*`, and adding a `--fill-destructive` namespace would have meant a theme-file change outside the item 1-2 surface; `currentColor` reuses the existing token.
- Bounded in-place fix, same defect class, same file: `markdown-theme.ts` also painted heading anchors, quote and meta tokens and blockquote border/background from bare `var(--muted-foreground)`, `var(--border)` and `var(--muted)` (all HSL triplets). They are wrapped in `hsl()` now. Evidence: the new pin's Markdown case asserts zero bare theme variables in that file and failed on the base tree (reverse check below).

**Item 3 (light danger text contrast), per the maintainer's ruling recorded on the card (comment 7052747252):**

> The light theme gets its own `--destructive-text` value, red-700 (`#b91c1c`). … `--text-color-destructive` then reads it. `--destructive`, the brand red used for button and badge fills, does not change.

- `:root` in all four shipped theme blocks sets `--destructive-text: 0 73.7% 41.8%` (red-700 in HSL, like its neighbours): `@object-ui/components`, the console, the runner, and the `objectui init` app template in the CLI's app generator (it has a full `:root`/`.dark` theme block, so it gets the same line). `--destructive` and `--destructive-foreground` are unchanged in both modes.
- `ThemeEngine` keeps `error` on the fill (`--destructive`, unchanged) and derives the danger text from it **per mode** (round 1 rework). Hue and saturation are the error colour's. Lightness moves down for light, or up for dark, only as far as 4.5:1 on that mode's extreme shipped surfaces needs (white and `240 18% 94%`; `222.2 84% 4.9%`, `217.2 32.6% 17.5%` and `240 5% 16%`). The values are written as `--destructive-text-light` and `--destructive-text-dark`, and each stylesheet's `:root` / `.dark` reads its own into `--destructive-text` (`var(--destructive-text-light, 0 73.7% 41.8%)`, `var(--destructive-text-dark, 0 91% 71%)`). Why this shape rather than passing the mode into the engine: `ThemeProvider` applies the vars once as inline style on the root, whatever the mode. A mode parameter on the exported `generateThemeVars`/`generateColorVars` would widen the published surface of `@object-ui/core` (Clause-② yes). Leaving the per-mode choice in CSS keeps every exported signature byte-for-byte and needs no re-apply on a mode switch: the `.dark` class flip alone re-resolves it, measured below. The engine never writes `--destructive-text` itself. A non-hex `error` derives nothing, and the stylesheet's own danger text applies. For `#EF4444`: fill `0 84% 60%`, light text `0 84.2% 45.7%`, dark text `0 84.2% 65.7%`.
- `content/docs/frontend/theming.mdx` names the light value and that the theme engine sets both tokens.
- Out of scope per the ruling and untouched: white text on the red button fill (3.59:1).
- Screenshot baselines: the tree has no pixel baselines for these surfaces (`git ls-files` finds no screenshot snapshot directories under `ui/`; the DOM snapshots in `components` carry class names, not computed colours, and still pass). Nothing to regenerate.

## Tests

- New `ui/packages/components/src/__tests__/destructive-colour-spelling-35911.test.ts`: scans every shipped `ui/packages/*/src` and `ui/apps/*/src` source (tests excluded) and fails on a bare `var(--destructive…)` used as a colour value and on any `fill-destructive`/`stroke-destructive`; asserts the Markdown theme's caution rules read the dark-aware token and that the file has no bare theme variable. A reach case asserts the scan covers the four files.
- `dark-danger-text-contrast-35658.test.ts`: its "light leaves `--destructive-text` unset" case pinned the decision the ruling reversed; it now asserts the light value is red-700, clears 4.5:1 on every light surface each stylesheet defines, and that the light `--destructive` is unchanged; the template case also pins the light value.
- `ThemeEngine.test.ts`: for five tenant reds (`#EF4444`, `#7C3AED`, `#F97316`, `#991B1B`, `#FCA5A5`) the derived light text clears 4.5:1 on every light surface the sheets define, the dark text clears it on every dark one, and both keep the error colour's hue. For `#EF4444`, neither text equals the fill. The engine never writes `--destructive-text`. No `error` colour, or a non-hex one, derives nothing.
- The `35658` pin reads the per-mode indirection (`:root` and `.dark` values are `var(--destructive-text-light|dark, FALLBACK)`, and contrast is checked on the fallback). The `35911` scan accepts a triplet custom property reading another triplet.

<details><summary>Readings</summary>

- Affected suites at head: `vitest run` over the new pin, the 35658 pin, `packages/plugin-markdown/`, `packages/core/src/theme/`, the CLI app-generator test and `FlowCanvas.test.tsx`: `Test Files 10 passed (10)`, `Tests 208 passed (208)` (lock VERDICT command-exit 0).
- Reverse check (fix committed; the nine source/theme files restored from base `09f6d457` with `git restore --source`, run, restored with `git checkout HEAD --`, `git diff HEAD` empty): `Tests 8 failed | 72 passed (80)` across the three pin files: both scan cases, the Markdown case, the light-value case (x3 sheets), the template case and the ThemeEngine custom-error case.
- `type-check` for `@object-ui/core`, `@object-ui/plugin-markdown`, `@object-ui/components`: exit 0.

- Round 1 head `ae2175e7`: the theme pins, `packages/core/src/theme/`, the CLI app-generator test and `ThemeProvider.test.tsx`: `Test Files 5 passed (5)`, `Tests 164 passed (164)`. Ablation: `ThemeEngine.ts` restored from the previous head `5136a763` (copy behaviour; on disk `deriveDangerTextVars` 0 hits, the copy 1 hit), ran `packages/core/src/theme/`: `Tests 7 failed | 62 passed (69)`. Restored with `git checkout HEAD --`; blob hash matches HEAD; `git diff HEAD` empty. `type-check` of `@object-ui/core` and `@object-ui/components`: exit 0.
- CI on round 1's first push `d725f33e`: `TypeScript Type Check`, `Lint & Repo Gates` and `Test UI` concluded red because every lane and shard under them was `cancelled` (`The operation was canceled.`, 00:21:13Z) when `ae2175e7` was pushed at about 00:20Z and superseded the run. No test failed there. `d725f33e` did carry one real defect, found locally before CI reached it: the `35911` scan flagged the new `--destructive-text: var(--destructive-text-light, …)` declarations (`Tests 1 failed | 163 passed`). `ae2175e7` fixes the scan, giving `164 passed`. CI on `ae2175e7`: 52 success, 10 skipped, 0 failed, including all eleven required contexts.

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- Read first, by risk: (1) the `:root` hunk in `ui/packages/components/src/index.css` (and its three copies): every `text-destructive` in light mode changes from `#ef4444` to `#b91c1c`; (2) `deriveDangerTextVars` in `ThemeEngine.ts` and the two `var(--destructive-text-light|dark, …)` lines per sheet: a themed tenant's danger text now follows its `error` hue in both modes, at ≥4.5:1; (3) the two FlowCanvas class swaps.
- Same family, not fixed here (outside the file surface): `metadata-viewer.tsx` in `@object-ui/components` falls back to a bare `var(--muted-foreground)` for its status dot colour. Reported to the seat with the family, not filed by this PR.
- Flow edge labels and badges for invalid edges keep `border-destructive/40-60` borders; their text is already `text-destructive` and readable in dark.
- Two-minute check: open a list, make an export fail (or open the harness below), and switch themes; the error line is red in both. In Studio, open a flow with a cycle: the red edge and arrowhead are bright red on dark.

## Verification

NOT MEASURED in the running console: booting the app for three surfaces would have cost more than the S card carries. Instead, a Chromium harness renders the three surfaces against the real `components` stylesheet compiled by Tailwind (before = base `09f6d457`, after = head), with the real Markdown theme CSS, and reads computed colours. Screenshots and the script: project files `build-seat1/35911/` (`before-light.png`, `before-dark.png`, `after-light.png`, `after-dark.png`, `measurements.txt`, `shoot.mjs`).

| Theme | Surface | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| light | export error | `rgb(2, 8, 23)` (inherited, not red) | `rgb(185, 28, 28)` 6.47:1 |
| dark | export error | `rgb(248, 250, 252)` (inherited) | `rgb(248, 114, 114)` 7.28:1 |
| light | caution title / border | inherited `rgb(2, 8, 23)` | `rgb(185, 28, 28)` 6.47:1 |
| dark | caution title / border | inherited `rgb(248, 250, 252)` | `rgb(248, 114, 114)` 7.28:1 |
| light | invalid edge + arrowhead | `rgb(239, 68, 68)` 3.76:1 | `rgb(185, 28, 28)` 6.47:1 |
| dark | invalid edge + arrowhead | `rgb(127, 29, 29)` 2.00:1 | `rgb(248, 114, 114)` 7.28:1 |

Tenant red `#EF4444` applied as inline vars on the root, as `ThemeProvider` does, with `.dark` toggled light → dark → light on the same page (`modeswitch.mjs`, `tenant-measurements.txt` and `tenant-*.png` in the same folder):

| Head | light | dark | light again |
|---|---|---|---|
| `5136a763` (copy) | `rgb(239,67,67)` 3.78:1 | `rgb(239,67,67)` 5.29:1 (this red happens to clear dark; a deep tenant red would not) | 3.78:1 |
| `ae2175e7` (per mode) | `rgb(215,18,18)` 5.27:1 | `rgb(241,94,94)` 6.20:1 | 5.27:1 |

The fill stays `rgb(239,67,67)` in both.
